title: How to update Chrome in Chrome on Mac: manual steps and troubleshooting for stable versions
metaTitle: How to update Chrome on Mac: Step-by-Step Guide
description: Learn how to update Chrome on Mac by checking the About menu. Follow these simple steps to ensure you are running the latest version of Google Chrome.
targetKeyword: how to update chrome on mac
intro: To update Chrome on your Mac, click the three-dot menu, select Help, and then click About Google Chrome to trigger an automatic check. The browser will then download any available updates and prompt you to relaunch to finish the process.
tldr: Open Google Chrome on your Mac.
Click the three-dot icon in the top-right corner.
Go to Help > About Google Chrome.
Wait for the update to download and click Relaunch.

blocks.text: Why you should keep Chrome updated

Keeping your browser updated is the primary way to protect your digital life. Security patches are released with every new version to close vulnerabilities that hackers might exploit. Beyond security, updates often improve how the browser handles modern web standards and media formats. You might notice your favorite websites loading faster or better battery life on your Mac after a major update.

Google maintains a consistent release cycle for its browser. Major versions typically arrive every six weeks. This rapid pace ensures that new features reach users quickly. However, it also means that if you leave your browser open for days on end, you might fall behind on these critical improvements. A quick check once a week is a good habit for any Mac user.

Chrome is designed to be self-maintaining. It uses a background process called GoogleSoftwareUpdate to check for new files periodically. When you close and reopen the browser, it usually applies these updates without you needing to do anything. If you are someone who keeps your computer running for weeks without a reboot, this background process might get stuck.

If you see a colored circle on the three-dot menu icon in the top-right corner, that is your signal. Green means an update has been waiting for two days. Orange means it has been waiting for four days. Red means the update has been pending for seven days or more. Do not ignore these colors, as they indicate that your browser is significantly outdated.

Sometimes the process does not go as planned. You might see errors like Error 3, 4, 7, 10, 11, or 12. These usually point to network issues or restrictive firewalls. If you use a VPN or a corporate security tool, it might be blocking the connection to the Google update servers. Try disabling your VPN temporarily to see if the update proceeds.

If you encounter Error 9, this is a file permission issue. Your Mac is preventing Chrome from modifying its own application folder. You can fix this by opening Terminal and running a command to take ownership of the application folder. Type 'sudo chown -R root:wheel /Applications/Google\ Chrome.app' and enter your Mac password. This resets the permissions and allows the update to proceed.

If nothing else works, a clean install is the most reliable path. Drag your current Chrome app to the Trash. Go to the official Google Chrome website and download a fresh installer. Install it as you would any other Mac application. This replaces the entire browser structure, including the update component, which often clears out any persistent corruption.

Chrome does not support every version of macOS forever. As of late 2026, you need at least macOS 13 Ventura to run the latest version. If you are still on an older system, you will be stuck on an older version of Chrome. This is a major security risk because those older versions no longer receive security patches.

If you cannot update your macOS, you should consider using a different browser that still supports your operating system, or look into upgrading your Mac hardware. Running an outdated browser on an outdated operating system makes your computer an easy target for malware. Always check your macOS version in the Apple menu under About This Mac.

Many users have multiple profiles for work and personal use. Each profile shares the same update status because they all run on the same core browser engine. You do not need to update each profile separately. Updating the main application updates everything across all your profiles. It is a shared ecosystem managed by the single Chrome application on your disk.

faq.question: How do I know if my Chrome is up to date?
faq.answer: Click the three-dot menu, select Help, and click About Google Chrome. It will tell you if your browser is up to date or if it is currently downloading an update.

faq.question: Why does Chrome say update failed?
faq.answer: This usually happens due to network restrictions or file permission errors. Check your firewall, VPN, or try a clean reinstall of the application.

faq.question: Does updating Chrome delete my bookmarks?
faq.answer: No, updating the browser does not delete your bookmarks, history, or saved passwords. These are stored in your user profile folder and remain untouched during the update process.

appliesTo: Google Chrome on macOS 13 or later

steps.name: Open Chrome
steps.text: Launch the Google Chrome browser from your Applications folder or Dock.

steps.name: Access the menu
steps.text: Look for the three-dot icon in the top-right corner of the window and click it.

steps.name: Navigate to About
steps.text: Hover your mouse over the Help option and click on About Google Chrome.
steps.tip: This opens a dedicated tab that checks for updates immediately.

steps.name: Wait for update
steps.text: Chrome will show a progress bar as it checks for and downloads the latest version.

steps.name: Relaunch
steps.text: Once the download completes, click the Relaunch button to apply the update.

troubleshooting.fix: Run 'sudo chown -R root:wheel /Applications/Google\ Chrome.app' in Terminal.
Delete the GoogleSoftwareUpdate folder in ~/Library/Google/ and restart the Mac.
Drag the app to Trash and download a fresh installer from google.com/chrome.
